headline: GOLD SLIDES TO $4,314 — Two-Month Low as Fed Rate-Hike Odds Jump to 72% on 172K Jobs Shock
snippet: Gold hit a two-month low of $4,313.99/oz on June 8, falling from Friday's $4,410 close as markets dramatically repriced Fed policy following May's blowout 172,000-jobs payroll print — nearly double the 85,000 consensus. Year-end rate-hike probability surged to 72%, erasing prior cut expectations and pressing gold through the $4,370 demand zone that technical analysts had flagged as a critical line between correction and breakdown. Central bank buying running at 244 tonnes in Q1 2026 provides the structural floor, but the speculative washout is ongoing.

headline: SILVER COILS AT $67.60 — Iran Launches 30 Missiles at Israel (War Day 100), But Rate-Hike Dread Caps the Rally
snippet: XAG/USD is pinned in a tight range at $67.60 on June 8 as two forces fight to a standstill: Iran launched roughly 30 ballistic missiles at Israel as the conflict's 100th day shattered the already fragile ceasefire, injecting fresh safe-haven demand into silver, while the prior week's 172K US jobs print keeps rate-hike odds elevated and the dollar bid. The $67–$70 band is the current battleground — a breakout either way would likely require a resolution on either the geopolitical or Fed policy front.

headline: WALL STREET KEEPS RAISING MP Materials Targets — Q1 Revenue Crushed Estimates $90M vs. $70M Forecast
snippet: Morgan Stanley raised its MP Materials (NYSE: MP) price target to $71 and BMO Capital lifted to $75 after Q1 2026 revenue of $90 million smashed the $70 million Wall Street estimate. Analysts are beginning to view MP less as a mining story and more as an integrated rare earth manufacturing platform, supported by a landmark U.S. government public-private partnership with a $110/kg NdPr price floor. William Blair also initiated coverage at Outperform, signalling growing institutional confidence in the domestic rare earth supply chain build-out.

headline: ENERGY FUELS' WHITE MESA MILL — America's Answer to China's Rare Earth Processing Dominance Takes Shape in Utah
snippet: A Deseret News investigation finds that Energy Fuels' White Mesa Mill in southeastern Utah — the U.S.'s last conventional uranium processing facility — is pivoting into one of the only scalable rare earth mineral processing plants in the country. Senior VP Curtis Moore describes it as 'truly a piece of critical infrastructure' with capabilities no other U.S. facility possesses. The mill has already demonstrated commercial production of separated light rare earths and is targeting commercial heavy rare earth oxide output, including terbium, by 2027.

headline: JEFFERIES WARNS: Iran-Driven $100/bbl Oil Could Lift Gold Miner AISC 5–9% — Open-Pit Africa Operations Face 30–40% Diesel Cost Exposure
snippet: Jefferies analyst Fahad Tariq warns that sustained oil at $90–$100/bbl — where prices have sat since the Iran conflict began — could push sector-wide all-in sustaining costs 5–9% above budgets built around $70/bbl oil. Open-pit operations in Africa and Latin America face 30–40% cost structure exposure to diesel, versus 4–5% for underground grid-connected mines. Consumables inflation typically lags oil by one to two quarters, making H2 2026 the key risk window for AISC revisions at Endeavour Mining, B2Gold, and OceanaGold.

headline: WEDA BAY NICKEL HALTS Production After 2026 Indonesian Quota Slashed to 12M Tonnes — Was 42M in 2025
snippet: Eramet has halted ore production at Weda Bay Nickel — its joint venture with China's Tsingshan and Indonesia's Antam — after exhausting a 2026 mining quota of just 12 million wet metric tonnes, down 71% from the 42 million tonnes produced in 2025. Indonesia controls 40–50% of global nickel mine supply and the deliberate quota tightening is designed to support domestic processing margins after years of oversupply. The halt removes a material volume from the global supply chain and is already being cited as a tailwind for nickel prices in H2 2026.

headline: ISS RECOMMENDS FOR G2 Goldfields / G Mining Venture Deal — 72% Premium, Proxy Deadline June 12, Vote June 16
snippet: Institutional Shareholder Services has recommended G2 Goldfields shareholders vote in favour of acquisition by G Mining Ventures at a 72% premium to 30-day VWAP. Under the terms, G2 shareholders receive 0.212 G Mining Ventures shares plus 0.5 shares of newly spun-out G3 Goldfields for each share held. The proxy deadline is June 12, the special shareholder meeting is June 16, and deal close is targeted for early July 2026, pending Canadian court approval and remaining conditions.

headline: USA RARE EARTH LOCKS IN $1.6 BILLION CHIPS Act Deal — Round Top Texas Mine + South Carolina NdFeB Magnet Plant
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) finalised agreements with the U.S. Department of Commerce on June 3 for up to $1.6 billion in CHIPS Act support — $277 million in direct grants and $1.3 billion in senior secured loans — to develop the Round Top heavy rare earth project in Sierra Blanca, Texas, and construct a sintered neodymium-iron-boron magnet manufacturing and refined metals plant in Cherokee County, South Carolina. The funding cements USAR's ambition to build a domestic mines-to-magnets supply chain targeting dysprosium and terbium that currently flows almost entirely through China.

headline: DRYDEN GOLD HITS 29.55 g/t Au Near Surface at Gold Rock — 2026 Drill Program Expanded to 45,000 Metres
snippet: Dryden Gold Corp. (TSXV: DRY) reported hole DGR-051 returning 3.24 g/t gold over 14.77 metres — including a 29.55 g/t Au core over 1.35 metres at just 88 metres depth — at the Sparrow target within the Big Master Gold System at Gold Rock, Ontario. The result prompted expansion of the 2026 drill program to 45,000 metres with a second rig deploying July 1, targeting both near-surface footprint and depth extensions of the system.

headline: SURGE BATTERY METALS Raises C$30 Million for Nevada North Lithium — Nasdaq Listing Planned Under 'Lithium X2' Name
snippet: Surge Battery Metals (TSXV: NILI) closed a C$30 million private placement at C$0.60 per unit, co-led by Brian Paes-Braga of SAF Group and Michael Hess of Hess Capital, both of whom join its strategic advisory board. The raise is earmarked to advance the Nevada North lithium project ahead of a planned U.S. Nasdaq listing under a proposed name change to Lithium X2 Mining, expected to close around June 20, 2026 — signalling a bet on continued institutional appetite for North American lithium development.
